      <code>api()</code>. If not passed, defaults to <code>true</code>.
    </p>
    <p>
      See{' '}
      <Link to="../factories/api#wrap">
        <code>api#wrap</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  </Item>
</Legend>}

## Methods

{<Legend>
  <Item name="addExports">
    <p>
      Accepts an object. The object can contain anything, though all properties
      should be stable references - memoized functions or ref objects that won't
      change on subsequent evaluations.
    </p>
    <p>
      Merges the passed object into any already-set{' '}
      <Link to="#exports">exports</Link> on this AtomApi. If no exports have
      been set yet on this AtomApi, <code>.addExports()</code> sets the exports.
    </p>
    <p>Returns the AtomApi for chaining.</p>
    <Ts>{`api('val')
  .addExports({ a: 1 })
  .addExports({ b: 2 })
  .addExports({ a: 3 })
  .exports // { a: 3, b: 2 }`}</Ts>
  </Item>
  <Item name="setExports">
    <p>
      The main way to set an AtomApi's exports. Accepts an object. The object
      can contain anything, though all properties should be stable references -
      memoized functions or ref objects that won't change on subsequent
      evaluations.
    </p>
    <p>Overwrites any previously-set exports on this AtomApi.</p>
    <p>
      If this AtomApi is returned from a state factory, these exports will be
      set as the atom instance's{' '}
      <Link to="AtomInstance#exports">
        <code>.exports</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
    <p>Returns the AtomApi for chaining.</p>
    <Ts>{`const initialExports = api(val).setExports({ ...myExports })
const overwriteExports = api(initialExports).setExports({ ...newExports })`}</Ts>
  </Item>
  <Item name="setPromise">
    <p>
      Accepts a promise. Sets the{' '}
      <Link to="#promise">
        <code>.promise</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      property of this AtomApi.
    </p>
    <p>
      If this AtomApi is returned from a state factory, the promise will be set
      as the atom instance's{' '}
      <Link to="AtomInstance#promise">
        <code>.promise</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      and will be used to cause React to suspend.
    </p>
    <p>
      This promise does not have to be a stable reference, though you should be
      conscious of when its reference changes since any components using the
      atom instance will re-suspend when the promise changes (if this AtomApi is
      returned from the state factory).
    </p>
    <p>Returns the AtomApi for chaining.</p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="setTtl">
    <p>
      Accepts an <Link to="../types/AtomInstanceTtl">AtomInstanceTtl</Link> or a
      function that returns an AtomInstanceTtl. This will be set as the
      AtomApi's <code>.ttl</code> property.
    </p>
    <p>
      If this AtomApi is returned from a state factory, this AtomInstanceTtl
      will be set as the atom instance's TTL, overriding any atom config and
      ecosystem-level TTL.
    </p>
    <p>Returns the AtomApi for chaining.</p>
  </Item>
</Legend>}

## See Also

- [The Atom APIs walkthrough](../../walkthrough/atom-apis)
- [`api()`](../factories/api)

---

# AtomInstance.mdx

Source: https://github.com/omnistac/zedux/blob/master/docs/docs/api/classes/AtomInstance.mdx

id: AtomInstance
title: AtomInstance

import useBaseUrl from '@docusaurus/useBaseUrl'
import {
  Legend,
  Item,
  Link,
  Sandbox,
  Tabs,
  Ts,
  tab1,
  tab2,
} from '@site/src/all'

export const AddDependentConfigParam = () => (
  <Item name="config">
    <p>Optional. An object containing the following optional properties:</p>
    <Ts>{`{ callback, operation }`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="callback">
        <p>
          A <Link to="../types/DependentCallback">DependentCallback</Link>{' '}
          function.
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="operation">
        <p>
          A string. Can be anything. This can be useful when debugging your
          selector graph. It essentially labels the edge, showing what operation
          caused the graph edge to be added.
        </p>
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
)

export const EvaluationReasonParams = ({ type = 'atom instance' }) => (
  <>
    <Item name="nextReasons">
      <p>
        An array that tracks the batched{' '}
        <Link to="../types/EvaluationReason">EvaluationReasons</Link> that will
        lead to the {type} reevaluating.
      </p>
      <p>
        If the {type} is currently evaluating, this is the list of reasons
        explaining why and is what{' '}
        <Link to="Ecosystem#why">
          <code>ecosystem.why()</code>
        </Link>{' '}
        will return.
      </p>
      <p>
        This will be empty if no reevaluation is currently scheduled or if this
        is the first evaluation of the {type}.
      </p>
    </Item>
    <Item name="prevReasons">
      <p>
        An array that tracks the batched{' '}
        <Link to="../types/EvaluationReason">EvaluationReasons</Link> describing
        why the {type} last evaluated. This will be empty if the last evaluation
        was the first.
      </p>
    </Item>
  </>
)

All standard atoms (aka "atom instances") are actually instances of this class. When Zedux instantiates [atom templates](AtomTemplate) (and [ion templates](IonTemplate)), it's just creating instances of this class.

## Creation

You should never instantiate this class yourself. Zedux does it for you. An instance is created the first time a given atom template + params combo is used.

Many hooks and injectors return instances of this class.

```ts
import { useAtomInstance } from '@zedux/react'
import { myAtom } from './atoms'

function MyComponent() {
  // creates the instance if it doesn't exist yet
  const instance = useAtomInstance(myAtom)
  ...
}
```

## Providing

An atom instance can be provided over React context via [`<AtomProvider>`](../components/AtomProvider).

```tsx
import { AtomProvider, useAtomInstance } from '@zedux/react'
import { myAtom } from './atoms'

function Parent() {
  const instance = useAtomInstance(myAtom)

  return (
    <AtomProvider instance={instance}>
      <Child />
    </AtomProvider>
  )
}
```

Consume provided instances with [`useAtomContext()`](../hooks/useAtomContext)

```ts
import { useAtomContext } from '@zedux/react'
import { myAtom } from './atoms'

function Child() {
  const instance = useAtomContext(myAtom)
}
```

## Extending

There are many aspects of an atom instance's behavior you can change when extending this class. This is an extremely advanced feature. We're not documenting it yet as the internals of this class may change.

## Properties

Atom instances have the following **readonly** properties:

{<Legend>
  <Item name="ecosystem">
    <p>
      A reference to the <Link to="Ecosystem">ecosystem</Link> that created and
      controls this atom instance.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="exports">
    <p>An object. May be undefined, if nothing was exported.</p>
    <p>
      The exports of the atom instance, as defined by the instance's returned{' '}
      <Link to="AtomApi">AtomApi</Link>.
    </p>
    <p>
      This object is stable. It is set the first time an atom instance is
      created and will not change on subsequent evaluations.
    </p>
    <Ts>{`import { api, atom } from '@zedux/react'\n
const exportsAtom = atom('exports', () => api().setExports({ hello: 'world' }))\n
const importAtom = atom('import', () => {
  const { hello } = injectAtomInstance(exportsAtom).exports
})`}</Ts>
  </Item>
  <Item name="id">
    <p>
      A string. This is the stable, unique id of this atom instance in the
      ecosystem. This id is the combination of the{' '}
      <Link to="AtomTemplate#key">atom template's key</Link> and a deterministic
      stringification of the{' '}
      <Link to="#params">
        <code>params</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      of this atom instance. Zedux uses this internally to identify this atom
      instance in the graph and atom instances cache.
    </p>
    <Ts>{`ecosystem.getInstance(atom('a', null)).id // 'a'
ecosystem.getInstance(
  atom('b', (param: string) => param),
  ['c']
).id // 'b-["c"]'`}</Ts>
  </Item>
  <EvaluationReasonParams />
  <Item name="params">
    <p>
      A reference to the raw, unserialized params that were used to create this
      atom instance. If the atom doesn't take params, this will be an empty
      array.
    </p>
    <Ts>{`const instanceA = useAtomInstance(myAtom, ['param 1', 'param 2'])
const instanceB = useAtomInstance(myAtom, ['a', 'b'])
instanceA.params // ['param 1', 'param 2']
instanceB.params // ['a', 'b']`}</Ts>
    <p>
      All params must be serializable (no functions or symbols)! This is because
      Zedux converts the params to a stable string representation in order to
      efficiently check for an existing atom instance with the "same" params.
    </p>
    <p>
      Sameness is determined by deep value comparison, not reference equality.
      Order matters!
    </p>
    <Ts>{`// These params are the "same" in Zedux's eyes:
useAtomInstance(myAtom, ['a', { b: 'b', c: 'c' }])
useAtomInstance(myAtom, ['a', { c: 'c', b: 'b' }])\n
// But these are different:
useAtomInstance(myAtom, ['a', 'b'])
useAtomInstance(myAtom, ['b', 'a'])`}</Ts>
    <p>
      The only exception to the serializable rule is other atom instances.
      That's right! You can pass an atom instance to another atom instance. You
      can then use{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomGetters#get">
        <code>get()</code>
      </Link>
      , <Link to="../injectors/injectAtomValue">
        <code>injectAtomValue()</code>
      </Link>, or any other dynamic injector to register a <Link to="../glossary#dynamic-graph-dependency">
        dynamic graph dependency
      </Link> on the passed atom instance.
    </p>
    <Sandbox
      ecosystemId="AtomInstance/shout"
      resultVar="Shout"
    >{`const normalAtom = atom(
  'normal',
  'row, row, row your boat gently lest I scream'
)\n
const shoutingAtom = atom(
  'shouting',
  (instance: AtomInstance<AtomGenericsPartial<{ State: string }>>) => {
    const val = injectAtomValue(instance) // subscribe to updates\n
    return val.toUpperCase()
  }
)\n
function Shout() {
  const instance = useAtomInstance(normalAtom)
  const shout = useAtomValue(shoutingAtom, [instance]) // just pass the instance\n
  return <div>{shout}</div>
}\n`}</Sandbox>
  </Item>
  <Item name="promise">
    <p>
      A promise. May be undefined if no promise was set on a returned{' '}
      <Link to="AtomApi">AtomApi</Link>.
    </p>
    <p>
      This promise will be used to cause React to suspend whenever this atom
      instance is used in a component until the promise completes. This promise
      reference will change if a subsequent evaluation returns a new promise.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="status">
    <p>A string representing the status of the atom instance:</p>
    <div>
      <img
        alt="Initializing -> Active <-> Stale -> Destroyed"
        src={useBaseUrl('/img/diagrams/status-machine.png')}
      />
    </div>
    <p>
      You typically shouldn't need to look at this but you may, for example,
      want to check that <code>instance.status !== 'Destroyed'</code> when
      holding a reference to an atom instance outside of React/atoms (and if it
      is, update your local reference using{' '}
      <Link to="Ecosystem#getinstance">ecosystem.getInstance()</Link>).
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="store">
    <p>
      A Zedux <Link to="Store">store</Link>. A reference to this atom instance's
      store. If the state factory returned a store, this is a reference to that
      store.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="template">
    <p>
      A reference to the <Link to="AtomTemplate">atom template</Link> that this
      atom instance was created from.
    </p>
  </Item>
</Legend>}

## Methods

{<Legend>
  <Item name="addDependent">
    <p>
      Manually adds a graph edge between this atom instance and a new external
      "pseudo" graph node. See the{' '}
      <Link to="../../walkthrough/destruction#manual-graphing">
        destruction walkthrough
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`addDependent = (config?) => cleanup`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <AddDependentConfigParam />
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="destroy">
    <p>
      Destroys the atom instance. Does nothing if the instance is already
      destroyed. Destruction bails out by default if the atom instance currently
      has dependents.
    </p>
    <p>
      Pass <code>true</code> to force destruction regardless of whether this
      atom instance has dependents. This will schedule a task to tell any
      dependents to automatically create a new instance after this one is
      destroyed.
    </p>
    <Ts>{`instance.destroy() // only destroy if not used elsewhere
instance.destroy(true) // force destruction`}</Ts>
    <p>
      See{' '}
      <Link to="../../walkthrough/destruction">
        the Destruction walkthrough
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="dispatch">
    <p>
      An alias for{' '}
      <Link to="Store#dispatch">
        <code>.store.dispatch()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="getState">
    <p>
      An alias for{' '}
      <Link to="Store#getstate">
        <code>.store.getState()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="invalidate">
    <p>Forces the atom instance to reevaluate.</p>
    <Sandbox
      ecosystemId="AtomInstance/invalidate"
      resultVar="Coin"
    >{`const coinTossAtom = atom('coinToss', () => Math.random() < 0.5)\n
function Coin() {
  const isHeads = useAtomValue(coinTossAtom)
  const { invalidate } = useAtomInstance(coinTossAtom)\n
  return <button onClick={invalidate}>{isHeads ? 'Heads' : 'Tails'}</button>
}`}</Sandbox>
    <p>
      A reference to this function is returned from{' '}
      <Link to="../injectors/injectInvalidate">
        <code>injectInvalidate()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="setState">
    <p>
      An alias for{' '}
      <Link to="Store#setstate">
        <code>.store.setState()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="setStateDeep">
    <p>
      An alias for{' '}
      <Link to="Store#setstatedeep">
        <code>.store.setStateDeep()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  </Item>
</Legend>}

# AtomTemplate.mdx

Source: https://github.com/omnistac/zedux/blob/master/docs/docs/api/classes/AtomTemplate.mdx

id: AtomTemplate
title: AtomTemplate

import { Legend, Item, Link, Tabs, Ts, tab1, tab2 } from '@site/src/all'

export const AtomKeyDesc = () => (
  <div>
    The key is the key to Dependency Injection - it's how ecosystems know which
    atom templates to override. It also aids development - many errors will log
    the key of the atom they originated in. Keys also help with a codebase's
    grepability.
  </div>
)

The object returned from [the `atom()` factory](../factories/atom). Instances of this class are passed to most of Zedux's hooks and injectors.

An atom template defines a skeleton that Zedux will use to create [atom instances](AtomInstance) on demand.

## Creation

Use [the `atom()` factory](../factories/atom) to create atom templates:

```ts
import { AtomTemplate, atom } from '@zedux/react'

const exampleAtom = atom('example', 'initial state')

exampleAtom instanceof AtomTemplate // true
```

:::note
The `_____Atom` naming convention comes from Jotai. If it's confusing (templates aren't atoms after all...), you don't have to use it. Feel free to pick your own.
:::

## Extending

When creating your own, custom atom types, you'll usually want to extend this class. Creating your own atom types is an advanced feature and we're not currently documenting it as the internals of these classes may change.

## Properties

{<Legend>
  <Item name="dehydrate">
    <p>A function. Can be undefined.</p>
    <p>
      A reference to the{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomConfig#dehydrate">
        <code>dehydrate</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      atom config option passed to{' '}
      <Link to="../factories/atom">
        <code>atom()</code>
      </Link>
      , if any.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="flags">
    <p>An array of strings. Can be undefined.</p>
    <p>
      A reference to the{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomConfig#flags">
        <code>flags</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      atom config option passed to{' '}
      <Link to="../factories/atom">
        <code>atom()</code>
      </Link>
      , if any.
    </p>
    <p>
      The flags that will be checked alongside an{' '}
      <Link to="Ecosystem#flags">ecosystem's flags</Link> to warn about unsafe
      atom templates being used in certain environments.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="hydrate">
    <p>A function. Can be undefined.</p>
    <p>
      A reference to the{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomConfig#hydrate">
        <code>hydrate</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      atom config option passed to{' '}
      <Link to="../factories/atom">
        <code>atom()</code>
      </Link>
      , if any.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="key">
    <p>A string.</p>
    <p>
      This is the key string passed as the first param to{' '}
      <Link to="../factories/atom">
        <code>atom()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
    <AtomKeyDesc />
  </Item>
  <Item name="manualHydration">
    <p>A boolean. Can be undefined.</p>
    <p>
      This is the{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomConfig#manualHydration">
        <code>manualHydration</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      atom config option passed to{' '}
      <Link to="../factories/atom">
        <code>atom()</code>
      </Link>
      , if any.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="ttl">
    <p>A number. Can be undefined.</p>
    <p>
      This is the{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomConfig#ttl">
        <code>ttl</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      atom config option passed to{' '}
      <Link to="../factories/atom">
        <code>atom()</code>
      </Link>
      , if any.
    </p>
    <p>
      If not set, the{' '}
      <Link to="Ecosystem#atomdefaults">
        ecosystem's <code>atomDefaults.ttl</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      will be used. If the ecosystem doesn't set a default, instances of this
      atom will live forever by default. Setting this value will override any
      default.
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>
        Set to <code>-1</code> to make this atom's instances live forever.
      </li>
      <li>
        Set to <code>0</code> to destroy all instances of this atom as soon as
        they go stale.
      </li>
      <li>
        Set to any positive integer to make atoms live in a stale state for{' '}
        <code>&lt;ttl&gt;</code> milliseconds before being cleaned up.
      </li>
    </ul>
    <p>
      This option can be overridden and configured more granularly by the atom
      instances themselves via{' '}
      <Link to="AtomApi#setttl">
        <code>AtomApi#setTtl()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  </Item>
</Legend>}

## Methods

{<Legend>
  <Item name="getInstanceId">
    <p>Gets a string id for a specific instance of this atom template.</p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`getInstanceId = (ecosystem, params?) => id`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Accepts an ecosystem and an array of atom params (required if the atom
      takes params, <code>undefined</code> if not). Uses the ecosystem's id
      generator to generate a predictable hash of the atom template's key +
      params combo.
    </p>
    <p>
      Zedux uses this internally to generate atom instance ids. You won't
      typically call this.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="override">
    <p>Creates a clone of this atom template, but with a different value.</p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`override = (newValue) => newAtom`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Accepts any of the same{' '}
      <Link to="../factories/atom#value">value types</Link> that{' '}
      <code>atom()</code> accepts. The state, promise, and exports type of the
      new value should match the corresponding types in the overridden atom.
      TypeScript will enforce this.
    </p>
    <p>Returns the new atom template.</p>
  </Item>
</Legend>}

## See Also

- [`atom()`](../factories/atom)
- [The Configuring Atoms walkthrough](../../walkthrough/configuring-atoms)

# Ecosystem.mdx

Source: https://github.com/omnistac/zedux/blob/master/docs/docs/api/classes/Ecosystem.mdx

id: Ecosystem
title: Ecosystem

import { Legend, Item, Link, Tabs, Ts, tab1, tab2 } from '@site/src/all'

The ecosystem is an isolated atom environment. Every ecosystem creates:

- A scheduler for intelligently running atom-related tasks.
- A graph that manages atom dependencies.
- A [Selectors](Selectors) class instance for managing cached [Atom Selectors](../types/AtomSelector).
- An id generator that generates unique ids for unnamed Atom Selectors and external graph nodes.

The Ecosystem class itself defines many methods for creating, destroying, and inspecting atom instances and the graph they form.

Ecosystems can be used completely outside of React. This can be helpful for testing atoms and selectors.

## Creation

Create ecosystems with [the `createEcosystem()` factory](../factories/createEcosystem).

```ts
import { createEcosystem } from '@zedux/react'

const rootEcosystem = createEcosystem({ id: 'root' })
```

Ecosystems are also created automatically when using an [`<EcosystemProvider>`](../components/EcosystemProvider) without passing an `ecosystem` prop:

```tsx
import { EcosystemProvider } from '@zedux/react'

function App() {
  return (
    <EcosystemProvider id="root">
      <Routes />
    </EcosystemProvider>
  )
}
```

Additionally, the [global ecosystem](../../walkthrough/ecosystems#global) will be created automatically if atoms are used in React outside any `<EcosystemProvider>`.

## Providing

Ecosystems can take control of all atom usages in a React component tree by wrapping the tree in [`<EcosystemProvider>`](../components/EcosystemProvider).

```tsx
function App() {
  return (
    <EcosystemProvider ecosystem={rootEcosystem}>
      <Routes />
    </EcosystemProvider>
  )
}
```

## Modifying Overrides

The ability to swap out atom implementations on the fly is one of Zedux's superpowers. Use [`.addOverrides`](#addoverrides), [`.removeOverrides`](#removeoverrides), or [`.setOverrides`](#setoverrides).

```tsx live ecosystemId=Ecosystem/modifying-overrides resultVar=Swapper
const one = atom('common-key', () => 'Numero Uno')
const two = atom('common-key', () => 'I am the best')
const three = atom('common-key', () => 'Two is not the best')

function Swapper() {
  const ecosystem = useEcosystem()
  const state = useAtomValue(one)

  return (
    <>
      <div>Current State: {state}</div>
      <button onClick={() => ecosystem.setOverrides([one])}>Use One</button>
      <button onClick={() => ecosystem.setOverrides([two])}>Use Two</button>
      <button onClick={() => ecosystem.setOverrides([three])}>Use Three</button>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Properties

All properties are readonly!

{<Legend>
  <Item name="atomDefaults">
    <p>
      An object. This is set to the <code>atomDefaults</code> value you passed
      via{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EcosystemConfig#atomdefaults">EcosystemConfig</Link>{' '}
      when creating this ecosystem.
    </p>
    <p>
      This object currently has a single optional property - <code>ttl</code>.
      This will be used as the ttl for all atom instances in the ecosystem that
      don't specify their own.
    </p>
    <p>
      If not set, <code>atomDefaults.ttl</code> defaults to <code>-1</code>,
      which means all atom instances in the ecosystem will live forever by
      default.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="complexParams">
    <p>
      A boolean. May be undefined. This is set to the <code>complexParams</code>{' '}
      value you passed via{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EcosystemConfig#complexparams">EcosystemConfig</Link>{' '}
      when creating this ecosystem.
    </p>
    <p>
      Whether to allow non-serializable values as atom and selector params. See{' '}
      <Link to="../../advanced/complex-params">the complex params guide</Link>.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="context">
    <p>
      An object. May be undefined. A reference to the `context` object passed to
      <Link to="../factories/createEcosystem">the <code>createEcosystem()</code> factory</Link>
      (if any) or the latest <Link to="#reset">
        <code>.reset</code>
      </Link> call. This object should be constant until the ecosystem is reset via
      <code>.reset()</code>.
    </p>
    <p>
      When <code>.reset()</code> is called, the previous context (if any) will
      be passed as the second parameter to{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EcosystemConfig#onready">
        the <code>onReady</code> function
      </Link>{' '}
      as part of the reset.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="destroyOnUnmount">
    <p>
      A boolean. May be undefined. This is set to the{' '}
      <code>destroyOnUnmount</code> value you passed via{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EcosystemConfig#destroyonunmount">
        EcosystemConfig
      </Link>{' '}
      when creating this ecosystem.
    </p>
    <p>
      This defaults to <code>false</code> for ecosystems created via{' '}
      <Link to="../factories/createEcosystem">
        <code>createEcosystem()</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      and to <code>true</code> for ecosystems automatically created when
      rendering an <code>&lt;EcosystemProvider&gt;</code> without passing an{' '}
      <code>ecosystem</code> prop.
    </p>
    <p>
      Whether to destroy this ecosystem when the last{' '}
      <Link to="../components/EcosystemProvider">
        <code>&lt;EcosystemProvider&gt;</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      providing it unmounts.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="id">
    <p>
      A string. The id of this ecosystem as set via{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EcosystemConfig#id">EcosystemConfig</Link> when
      creating this ecosystem. The string <code>'@@global'</code> is reserved
      for the global ecosystem.
    </p>
    <p>
      If you didn't specify an id when creating this ecosystem, this will be a
      randomly-generated string.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="flags">
    <p>
      An array of strings. This is set to the <code>flags</code> value you
      passed via{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EcosystemConfig#flags">EcosystemConfig</Link> when
      creating this ecosystem.
    </p>
    <p>
      These work in conjunction with{' '}
      <Link to="AtomTemplate#flags">atom flags</Link> to raise warnings when
      unsafe atom templates are not overridden in certain environments.
    </p>
    <p>
      If an atom template is used that has a flag that is not present in this
      array, Zedux will log a warning.
    </p>
    <p>
      Flag checking is off by default - simply don't pass a flags array to{' '}
      <code>createEcosystem()</code> and Zedux will ignore all flags. To turn it
      on, but with no flags, pass an empty array.
    </p>
    <Ts>{`createEcosystem() // flag checking disabled. Zedux will ignore all atom flags.
createEcosystem({ flags: [] }) // flag checking enabled! All flags will log warnings
createEcosystem({ flags: ['a'] }) // all atom flags except 'a' will log warnings
`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Which atoms, which flags, and which environments, is all up to you. You
      may want to flag atoms that run side effects you don't want to run in
      tests. Or you may want to flag atoms that use APIs that only work in the
      browser or in electron or any other environment.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="hydration">
    <p>
      An object. May be undefined. The shallowly merged result of all calls to{' '}
      <code>ecosystem.hydrate()</code> minus any keys that have been consumed
      already.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="modBus">
    <p>
      A <Link to="Store">Zedux Store</Link>. This store has no state. It serves
      only as a message bus for notifying plugins of mod events.
    </p>
    <p>
      See <Link to="../../advanced/plugins">the plugins guide</Link>.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="onReady">
    <p>
      A function. May be undefined. This is set to the <code>onReady</code>{' '}
      value you passed via{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EcosystemConfig#onready">EcosystemConfig</Link> when
      creating this ecosystem.
    </p>
    <p>
      Will be called as soon as the ecosystem has initialized. Is also called
      every time the ecosystem is{' '}
      <Link to="../classes/Ecosystem#reset">reset</Link>.
    </p>
    <p>
      This is the ideal place to bootstrap data and preload atoms. Since this
      function is called on reset, it can be used to ensure the ecosystem's
      "necessary data" is always loaded.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`(ecosystem, prevContext?) => maybeCleanup`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="ecosystem">A reference to this ecosystem</Item>
      <Item name="prevContext">
        <p>
          A reference to the previous context value of the ecosystem.{' '}
          <code>ecosystem.reset()</code> can be optionally given a new context
          object. If that happens, the ecosystem's context will be updated
          before this function is called. So a reference to the old context is
          passed here.
        </p>
        <p>
          This parameter will be undefined the first time <code>onReady</code>{' '}
          runs. Thus you can use this to check if this is the initial run.
        </p>
        <Ts>{`const ecosystem = createEcosystem({
  context: { redux: reduxStore },
  onReady: (ecosystem, prevContext) => {
    if (!prevContext) {
      // this is the initial run
    } else {
      // onReady is running after an ecosystem reset
      const nextContext = ecosystem.context
      
      if (prevContext.redux !== nextContext.redux) {
        // ecosystem.reset() changed the redux store reference
      }
    }
  }
})\n
ecosystem.reset() // doesn't change context (prevContext === ecosystem.context)
ecosystem.reset({ redux: otherReduxStore }) // replaces context`}</Ts>{' '}
        <p>
          Note that replacing context is an all-or-nothing deal. Spread{' '}
          <code>ecosystem.context</code> into a new object to update only part
          of the context:
        </p>{' '}
        <Ts>{`ecosystem.reset({ ...ecosystem.context, specialField: 'new val' })`}</Ts>
      </Item>
      <Item name="Returns">
        Either <code>undefined</code> or a cleanup function that will be called
        when the ecosystem is reset or destroyed.
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="overrides">
    <p>
      An object mapping atom keys to atom templates. These are the
      currently-overridden atoms in this ecosystem. Modify this list by calling{' '}
      <code>ecosystem.setOverrides()</code>,{' '}
      <code>ecosystem.addOverrides()</code>, and{' '}
      <code>ecosystem.removeOverrides()</code>.
    </p>
    <p>
      If an initial <code>overrides</code> array is passed, they will be
      immediately mapped into this object.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="selectors">
    <p>
      The <Link to="Selectors">Selectors</Link> class instance that tracks all
      cached atom selectors in this ecosystem.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="ssr">
    <p>
      A boolean. Whether the ecosystem is being used on the server to generate
      SSR content.{' '}
    </p>
    <p>
      This is set to the <code>ssr</code> value you passed via{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EcosystemConfig">EcosystemConfig</Link> when creating
      this ecosystem. If not specified, defaults to false.
    </p>
    <p>
      Currently the only thing this affects is <code>injectEffect()</code> - SSR
      mode prevents effects from running at all in this ecosystem.
    </p>
  </Item>
</Legend>}

## Methods

{<Legend>
  <Item name="addOverrides">
    <p>
      Adds new overrides to the ecosystem's current list of overrides and/or
      updates existing overrides - swapping them out with different
      implementations. All existing instances that match atom templates in the
      passed list will be force-destroyed, allowing their dependents to recreate
      them.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`addOverrides = (overrides) => void`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="overrides">
        Required. An array of <Link to="AtomTemplate">atom templates</Link>.
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="batch">
    <p>
      Accepts a callback and batches all updates that happen synchronously while
      the callback is running. Flushes all updates once the passed callback
      completes.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`batch = (callback) => void`}</Ts>
    <p>
      See <Link to="../../advanced/batching">the batching guide</Link>.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="dehydrate">
    <p>
      Returns a snapshot of the current state of instances in the ecosystem.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`dehydrate = ({
  exclude?,
  excludeFlags?,
  include?,
  includeFlags?,
  transform?
}) => snapshot`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="exclude">
        <p>
          Optional. An array of atom templates and/or case-insensitive
          fuzzy-search strings.
        </p>
        <p>
          Any atom instances of the passed atom templates or whose id matches
          any of the passed strings will be excluded from the snapshot.
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="excludeFlags">
        <p>Optional. An array of strings.</p>
        <p>
          Any atom instance whose template's{' '}
          <Link to="AtomTemplate#flags">flags</Link> contain any of the passed
          strings will be excluded from the snapshot.
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="include">
        <p>
          Optional. An array of atom templates and/or case-insensitive
          fuzzy-search strings.
        </p>
        <p>
          Only atom instances of the passed atom templates or whose ids match
          any of the passed strings will be included in the snapshot.
        </p>
        <p>
          Excludes take priority over includes - if an atom instance is excluded
          via <code>excludes</code> or <code>excludeFlags</code> <i>and</i>{' '}
          included here, it will still be excluded.
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="includeFlags">
        <p>Optional. An array of strings.</p>
        <p>
          Only atom instance whose template's{' '}
          <Link to="AtomTemplate#flags">flags</Link> contain any of the passed
          strings will be included in the snapshot.
        </p>
        <p>
          Excludes take priority over includes - if an atom instance is excluded
          via <code>excludes</code> or <code>excludeFlags</code> <i>and</i>{' '}
          included here, it will still be excluded.
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="transform">
        <p>
          Optional. A boolean. Default: <code>true</code>.
        </p>
        <p>
          Whether to transform state by passing it to{' '}
          <Link to="../types/AtomConfig#dehydrate">
            <code>dehydrate</code> atom config options
          </Link>
          .
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="Returns">
        <p>
          An object mapping atom instance ids to the transformed form (unless{' '}
          <code>transform: false</code>) of their current state.
        </p>
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="destroy">
    <p>
      Destroys all atom instances in the ecosystem, cleans up the ecosystem
      itself (e.g. by removing all currently scheduled tasks), and removes it
      from the <Link to="../utils/internal-utils#store">internal store</Link>.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`destroy = (force?) => void`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="force">
        <p>
          Optional. A boolean. Default: <code>false</code>.
        </p>
        <p>
          By default, destruction will bail out if this ecosystem is currently
          being used in any{' '}
          <Link to="../components/EcosystemProvider">
            <code>&lt;EcosystemProvider&gt;s</code>
          </Link>
          . Pass true to force destruction anyway. It is not recommended to pass
          this in a normal app.
        </p>
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="find">
    <p>
      Works similar to{' '}
      <Link to="#getinstance">
        <code>ecosystem.getInstance()</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      except it does NOT create the atom instance if it doesn't exist. In that
      case, <code>.find()</code> returns undefined.
    </p>
    <Ts>{`// creates the atom instance if needed:
instance = ecosystem.getInstance(myAtom, [...params])\n
// never creates an atom instance:
instance = ecosystem.find(myAtom, [...params])`}</Ts>
    <p>
      <code>.find()</code> can also take a fuzzy search string:
    </p>
    <Ts>{`instance = ecosystem.find('myAtomKey')`}</Ts>
    <p>
      In this case, <code>.find()</code> returns the first atom instance it
      finds whose id contains the passed string (case-insensitive), unless an
      exact match is found, in which case the exact-matching instance will be
      returned.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="findAll">
    <p>Get all atom instances in the ecosystem.</p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`findAll = (atom?) => instances`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="atom">
        An atom template or fuzzy search string. If an atom template is passed,{' '}
        <code>.findAll()</code> returns only instances of the passed template.
        If a string is passed, <code>.findAll()</code> returns only instances
        whose id includes the passed string (case-insensitive).
      </Item>
      <Item name="Returns">
        An object of all Active and Stale atom instances in the ecosystem, keyed
        by the instance's id.
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="get">
    <p>
      Gets the current value of an atom instance's store. Creates the atom
      instance if it doesn't exist yet. See{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomGetters#get">
        the <code>get</code> AtomGetter
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
    <Ts>{`const currentValue = myEcosystem.get(myAtom)
const withParams = myEcosystem.get(paramsAtom, ['param 1', 'param 2'])`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Note that this method - like all AtomGetters on the ecosystem - never
      registers graph dependencies, no matter where it's used.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="getInstance">
    <p>
      Gets an atom instance. Creates it if it doesn't exist yet. Set{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomGetters#getinstance">
        the <code>getInstance</code> AtomGetter
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
    <Ts>{`const instance = rootEcosystem.getInstance(myAtom)
const withParams = rootEcosystem.getInstance(paramsAtom, ['param 1', 'param 2'])\n
instance.getState()
instance.setState('new state')`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Note that this method - like all AtomGetters on the ecosystem - never
      registers graph dependencies, no matter where it's used.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="hydrate">
    <p>
      Hydrates the state of atom instances in this ecosystem, usually using a
      previous state snapshot from{' '}
      <Link to="#dehydrate">
        <code>ecosystem.dehydrate()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
    <p>
      If <code>.hydrate()</code> has been called before, the new hydration will
      be shallowly merged into the existing hydration.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`hydrate = (snapshot, config?) => void`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="snapshot">
        <p>
          Required. An object. The keys of this object are ids corresponding to
          atom instances that may or may not exist in the ecosystem yet.
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="config">
        <p>Optional. An object containing the following optional property:</p>
        <Ts>{`{ retroactive }`}</Ts>
        <p>
          By default, Zedux will update the state of all existing atom instances
          that have an entry in the passed snapshot. To disable this, pass{' '}
          <code>{`{ retroactive: false }`}</code>.
        </p>
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="registerPlugin">
    <p>
      Registers a plugin with this ecosystem. Does nothing if the plugin has
      already been registered. See{' '}
      <Link to="../../advanced/plugins">the plugins guide</Link>.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`registerPlugin = (plugin) => void`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Accepts a single <Link to="ZeduxPlugin">ZeduxPlugin</Link> instance.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="removeOverrides">
    <p>
      Removes overrides previously set via <code>.addOverrides()</code> or{' '}
      <code>.setOverrides()</code>. All existing instances of atom templates in
      the passed list will be force-destroyed, allowing their dependents to
      recreate them using the original, non-overridden atom template.
    </p>
    <p>
      You can pass either the original template or the override. Zedux only
      looks at their <code>key</code> properties. You can also pass strings
      matching atom template keys.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`removeOverrides = (overrides) => void`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="overrides">
        Required. An array of <Link to="AtomTemplate">atom templates</Link>{' '}
        and/or template key strings. If any haven't been set as overrides
        previously, they'll be ignored.
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="reset">
    <p>
      Wipes the ecosystem - force destroying all atom instances and cached
      selectors - calls the cleanup function returned from{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EcosystemConfig#onready">
        the <code>onReady</code> function
      </Link>{' '}
      (if any), and calls <code>onReady</code> again to reinitialize the
      ecosystem.
    </p>
    <p>
      Note that this doesn't remove overrides or plugins but <i>does</i> remove
      hydrations. This is because you can remove overrides/plugins yourself if
      needed, but there isn't currently a way to remove hydrations.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`reset = (newContext?) => void`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Takes an optional <code>newContext</code> object that will be passed to{' '}
      <code>onReady</code> and set as the new{' '}
      <Link to="#context">
        <code>.context</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      value of the ecosystem.
    </p>
    <Ts>{`const myEcosystem = createEcosystem({
  context: { someField: 'some val' },
  id: 'my',
  onReady: (ecosystem, prevContext) =>
    console.log('old context:', prevContext, 'new context:', ecosystem.context),
})
// old context: undefined new context: { someField: 'some val' }\n
myEcosystem.reset({ someField: 'new val' })
// old context: { someField: 'some val' } new context: { someField: 'new val' }`}</Ts>
  </Item>
  <Item name="select">
    <p>
      Gets the current value of a cached atom selector. If the atom selector
      hasn't been cached yet, runs the selector but does <i>not</i> cache the
      result. Use{' '}
      <Link to="Selectors#getcache">
        <code>ecosystem.selectors.getCache()</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      to create and cache a selector. See{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomGetters#select">
        the <code>select</code> AtomGetter
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
    <Ts>{`const selection = myEcosystem.select(myAtomSelector)
const withArgs = myEcosystem.select(myAtomSelector, 'param 1', 'param 2')`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Note that this method - like all AtomGetters on the ecosystem - never
      registers graph dependencies, no matter where it's used.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="setOverrides">
    <p>
      Replaces the ecosystem's list of overridden atoms with the passed
      overrides. All instances of atom templates in either the new or old lists
      will be force-destroyed, allowing their dependencies to recreate them.
    </p>
    <p>
      To selectively update only certain atoms, use{' '}
      <Link to="#addoverrides">
        <code>.addOverrides</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      or{' '}
      <Link to="#removeoverrides">
        <code>.removeOverrides</code>
      </Link>
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`setOverrides = (newOverrides) => void`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Accepts an array of atom templates. This will be set as the new{' '}
      <Link to="#overrides">
        <code>.overrides</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      property.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="unregisterPlugin">
    <p>
      Removes a plugin from the ecosystem. Calls the cleanup returned from the
      plugin's{' '}
      <Link to="ZeduxPlugin#registerecosystem">
        <code>registerEcosystem</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      function (if any), and turns off any mods the plugin enabled in the
      ecosystem that are not also requested by any other plugins.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`unregisterPlugin = (plugin) => void`}</Ts>
    <p>
      Accepts a single <Link to="ZeduxPlugin">ZeduxPlugin</Link> instance. If
      the plugin hasn't previously been registered via{' '}
      <Link to="#registerplugin">
        <code>.registerPlugin()</code>
      </Link>
      , it will be ignored.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="viewGraph">
    <p>
      See what the ecosystem's atom graph currently looks like. There are 3 ways
      to view the graph:
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>Top-down</li>
      <li>Bottom-up</li>
      <li>Flat</li>
    </ul>
    <p>
      Flat is the default and is the most useful. It returns a normalized object
      containing every node in the graph. Each node points to its dependencies
      and dependents in the top-level object.
    </p>
    <p>
      Top-down and bottom-up are mostly just for fun, to quickly gain some
      insight into what your dependency graph actually looks like. However,
      these views don't show "pseudo-nodes" (nodes that Zedux creates to
      represent external dependents like React components).
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`viewGraph = (view) => graph`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="view">
        Optional. One of <code>'flat'</code>, <code>'top-down'</code>, or{' '}
        <code>'bottom-up'</code>. Default: <code>'flat'</code>.
      </Item>
      <Item name="Returns">
        An object whose structure depends on the requested view. See{' '}
        <Link to="../../walkthrough/the-graph#getting-the-graph">
          the graph walkthrough
        </Link>
        .
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="why">
    <p>
      Returns a list of{' '}
      <Link to="../types/EvaluationReason">EvaluationReasons</Link> detailing
      why the current atom instance or selector is evaluating.
    </p>
    <p>
      If called outside a selector or atom state factory,{' '}
      <code>ecosystem.why()</code> always returns undefined.
    </p>
    <p>
      If this is the first evaluation of the current atom instance or selector,{' '}
      <code>ecosystem.why()</code> returns an empty array.
    </p>
  </Item>
</Legend>}

- [the `createEcosystem()` factory](../factories/createEcosystem)
- [the Overrides walkthrough](../../walkthrough/overrides)
- [the Plugins guide](../../advanced/plugins)

# IonTemplate.mdx

Source: https://github.com/omnistac/zedux/blob/master/docs/docs/api/classes/IonTemplate.mdx

id: IonTemplate
title: IonTemplate

Extends [AtomTemplate](AtomTemplate).

Ions are a specialized atom type. They excel at selector-type operations. The only difference from normal atoms is that an ion's [state factory](../glossary#state-factory) receives an [AtomGetters object](../types/AtomGetters) as its first parameter. All other params work exactly the same as normal atom params.

Unlike atoms, ions _must_ be given a state factory function. That's the whole point!

## Creation

Create ion templates using [the `ion()` factory](../factories/ion).

```ts
import { ion } from '@zedux/react'

const selectorAtom = ion('selector', ({ get }) => get(otherAtom).someField)
const derivedAtom = ion('derived', ({ get }) => deriveStuff(get(otherAtom)))

const withParams = ion('withParams', ({ get }, one: string, two: number) => {
  return `${one} ${two}`
})

const withInjectors = ion('withInjectors', ({ get }) => {
  // any injector can be used in the "getter" function.
  const val = injectMemo(() => getExpensiveVal(), [])

  return val
})

const withConfig = ion('withConfig', stateFactory, {
  flags: ['my-flag'],
  ttl: 0,
})
```

Ions expose no unique properties or methods besides those exposed by [AtomTemplate](AtomTemplate).

## See Also

- [the `AtomTemplate` class](AtomTemplate)
- [the Selectors walkthrough](../../walkthrough/selectors)

---

# SelectorCache.mdx

Source: https://github.com/omnistac/zedux/blob/master/docs/docs/api/classes/SelectorCache.mdx

id: SelectorCache
title: SelectorCache

import { Legend, Item, Link, Tabs, Ts, tab1, tab2 } from '@site/src/all'
import { EvaluationReasonParams } from './AtomInstance.mdx'

Every time an [ecosystem](Ecosystem)'s [`.selectors`](Selectors) manager caches an atom selector, the "cached selector" is really just an instance of this class. Thus, an instance of this class is what's returned from various Selectors class methods like [`.getCache()`](Selectors#getcache) and [`.findAll()`](Selectors#findall).

This class has no special functionality. It just stores data. It has to be a class (not any old object) so that Zedux can detect instances of it for certain APIs.

## Example

```ts live resultVar=cacheItem
const ecosystem = createEcosystem({ id: 'selector-cache-item-example' })
const numbersAtom = atom('numbers', () => [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])

const getOddNumbers = ({ get }: AtomGetters) =>
  get(numbersAtom).filter(num => num % 2)

const cacheItem = ecosystem.selectors.getCache(getOddNumbers)
```

## Properties

{<Legend>
  <Item name="args">
    <p>
      An array or undefined if this selector wasn't given args. This array
      contains references to the actual args passed, in the order passed.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="id">
    <p>
      A string. The id Zedux uses to refer to this SelectorCache in the{' '}
      <Link to="Selectors">Selectors</Link> class and the ecosystem graph.
    </p>
    <p>
      Contains a deterministic hash of all the selector's args and a name
      generated from the selector's function name if possible or the{' '}
      <Link to="../types/AtomSelectorConfig">AtomSelectorConfig</Link>'s{' '}
      <code>.name</code> property if given.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="isDestroyed">
    <p>
      A boolean or undefined. Cached atom selectors don't have a real lifecycle
      like <Link to="AtomInstance#status">atom instances</Link>. This is all
      they get.
    </p>
    <p>
      This will be set to true when the selector's ref count goes from 1 to 0
      and Zedux will discard all references to this object, allowing it to be
      garbage collected. If you're ever using an instance of this class where{' '}
      <code>isDestroyed</code> is true, you're doing something wrong. Consider
      using{' '}
      <Link to="../../walkthrough/destruction#manual-graphing">
        manual graphing
      </Link>{' '}
      to prevent automatic destruction and handle force destruction of
      SelectorCaches you're using outside React/atoms.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <EvaluationReasonParams type="selector" />
  <Item name="result">
    <p>
      The cached return value of the atom selector. Selectors don't use{' '}
      <Link to="Store">stores</Link>, this mutable value just sits right here.
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="selectorRef">
    <p>
      A reference to the actual selector function or AtomSelectorConfig object
      used to generate this selector cache item
    </p>
  </Item>
</Legend>}

## See Also

- [The Selectors walkthrough](../../walkthrough/selectors)
- [The `Selectors` class](Selectors)

---

# Selectors.mdx

Source: https://github.com/omnistac/zedux/blob/master/docs/docs/api/classes/Selectors.mdx

id: Selectors
title: Selectors

import { Legend, Item, Link, Tabs, Ts, tab1, tab2 } from '@site/src/all'
import { AddDependentConfigParam } from './AtomInstance.mdx'

The Selectors class manages all selector-related tasks for the ecosystem.

Since [atom selectors](../types/AtomSelector) are meant to feel lightweight, they don't have to be instances of a class - they'll often be standalone or even inline functions. This class handles all the logic that atom selectors would handle themselves if they were classes - instantiation, cache management, and destruction.

On top of that, it provides methods for pre-caching selectors and finding selector caches.

Every ecosystem creates a single Selectors instance - [`ecosystem.selectors`](Ecosystem#selectors).

## Methods

{<Legend>
  <Item name="addDependent">
    <p>
      Manually adds a graph edge between an atom selector and a new external
      "pseudo" graph node.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`addDependent = (cacheItem, config?) => cleanup`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="cacheItem">
        <p>
          Required. A <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache</Link> instance.
        </p>
        <p>This is the dependency you're adding a dependent to.</p>
      </Item>
      <AddDependentConfigParam />
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="dehydrate">
    <p>Gets a snapshot of current cache item values.</p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`dehydrate = (selectableOrName?) => cacheItems`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="selectableOrName">
        <p>Optional. One of:</p>
        <ul>
          <li>A string</li>
          <li>
            An <Link to="../types/AtomSelector">atom selector</Link>
          </li>
          <li>
            An{' '}
            <Link to="../types/AtomSelectorConfig">
              AtomSelectorConfig object
            </Link>
          </li>
          <li>
            A <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache instance</Link> (accepted
            for consistency, but really you'd never pass this)
          </li>
        </ul>
        <p>
          If passed, filters the returned object to only contain cache values of
          the passed selector or caches whose key includes the passed string
          (case-insensitive).
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="Returns">
        Returns an object mapping fully qualified SelectorCache ids to the
        cached result for that selector + params combo.
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="destroyCache">
    <p>
      Destroys a cached atom selector. Similar to{' '}
      <Link to="AtomInstance#destroy">
        <code>instance.destroy()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
    <p>
      Like <code>instance.destroy()</code>, destruction bails out by default if
      the selector node has dependents. Pass <code>true</code> as the 3rd
      parameter to force destruction anyway, triggering dependents to recreate
      the cache.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`destroyCache = (selectable, args?, force?) => void`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="selectable">
        <p>
          Required. An <Link to="../types/AtomSelector">atom selector</Link>,{' '}
          <Link to="../types/AtomSelectorConfig">
            AtomSelectorConfig object
          </Link>
          , or <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache instance</Link>.
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="args">
        An array. Required if the passed atom selector or AtomSelectorConfig
        object takes args. Otherwise (or when passing a SelectorCache instance),
        don't pass this or pass an empty array.
      </Item>
      <Item name="force">
        Optional. A boolean. Whether to force destruction regardless of whether
        the cached selector still has dependents.
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="find">
    <p>
      Similar to{' '}
      <Link to="#getcache">
        <code>selectors.getCache()</code>
      </Link>
      , returns a <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache</Link> instance for the
      given selector + args combo. However, unlike <code>.getCache()</code>, <code>
        .find()
      </code> does not run the selector or cache the result if it hasn't been cached
      already - it simply returns undefined.
    </p>
    <p>
      Signature is almost the same as{' '}
      <Link to="#getcache">
        <code>.getCache()</code>
      </Link>
      , except that <code>.find()</code> also accepts a fuzzy search string which,
      when passed, returns the first found SelectorCache whose id includes the passed
      string (case-insensitive).
    </p>
  </Item>
  <Item name="findAll">
    <p>
      Gets a snapshot of current cache items. The selector equivalent of{' '}
      <Link to="Ecosystem#findall">ecosystem.findAll()</Link>.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`findAll = (selectableOrName?) => cacheItems`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="selectableOrName">
        <p>Optional. One of:</p>
        <ul>
          <li>A string</li>
          <li>
            An <Link to="../types/AtomSelector">atom selector</Link>
          </li>
          <li>
            An{' '}
            <Link to="../types/AtomSelectorConfig">
              AtomSelectorConfig object
            </Link>
          </li>
          <li>
            A <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache instance</Link> (accepted
            for consistency with similar methods, but really you'd never pass
            this)
          </li>
        </ul>
        <p>
          If passed, filters the returned object to only contain caches of the
          passed selector or caches whose key includes the passed string
          (case-insensitive).
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="Returns">
        Returns an object mapping fully qualified SelectorCache ids to their{' '}
        <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache</Link> instances.
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="getCache">
    <p>
      Returns a <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache</Link> instance for the
      given selector + args combo. If the selector + args combo has never been
      cached before, <code>.getCache()</code> runs the selector and caches the
      result before returning the cache item.
    </p>
    <p>
      Contrast this to{' '}
      <Link to="Ecosystem#select">
        <code>ecosystem.select()</code>
      </Link>{' '}
      which does not cache the result. That means{' '}
      <code>selectors.getCache()</code> is the selector equivalent of{' '}
      <Link to="Ecosystem#getinstance">
        <code>ecosystem.getInstance()</code>
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`getCache = (selectable, args?) => cacheItem`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="selectable">
        <p>
          Required. An <Link to="../types/AtomSelector">atom selector</Link>,{' '}
          <Link to="../types/AtomSelectorConfig">
            AtomSelectorConfig object
          </Link>
          , or <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache instance</Link>.
        </p>
        <p>
          <code>.getCache()</code> has no special functionality if a
          SelectorCache instance is passed - it simply returns the passed cache
          item.
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="args">
        An array. Required if the passed atom selector or AtomSelectorConfig
        object takes args. Otherwise (or when passing a SelectorCache instance),
        don't pass this or pass an empty array.
      </Item>
      <Item name="Returns">
        A <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache</Link> instance.
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
  <Item name="getCacheId">
    <p>
      Returns the fully qualified id string that this Selectors class instance
      will use for the given selector + args combo.
    </p>
    <p>Signature:</p>
    <Ts>{`getCacheId = (selectable, args?, weak?) => id`}</Ts>
    {<Legend>
      <Item name="selectable">
        <p>
          Required. An <Link to="../types/AtomSelector">atom selector</Link>,{' '}
          <Link to="../types/AtomSelectorConfig">
            AtomSelectorConfig object
          </Link>
          , or <Link to="SelectorCache">SelectorCache instance</Link>.
        </p>
      </Item>
      <Item name="args">
        An array. Required if the passed atom selector or AtomSelectorConfig
        object takes args. Otherwise (or when passing a SelectorCache instance),
        don't pass this or pass an empty array.
      </Item>
      <Item name="weak">
        Optional. A boolean. By default, <code>.getCacheId()</code> creates and
        stores an id for the given selector + args combo if none exists yet.
        Pass <code>true</code> to disable this.
      </Item>
      <Item name="Returns">
        <p>
          A string prefixed with <code>@@selector-</code> containing a set,
          derived, or generated name for the passed selector and a deterministic
          hash of all the passed args. If <code>true</code> was passed for the
          3rd "weak" arg, returns undefined if no id has been stored for given
          selector + args combo yet.
        </p>
      </Item>
    </Legend>}
  </Item>
</Legend>}

## See Also

- [The Selectors walkthrough](../../walkthrough/selectors)
- [The `SelectorCache` class](SelectorCache)
